newsitem.title: UK: Shell to allow observers at Camisea gas project.
newsitem.headline: Shell to allow observers at Camisea gas project.

text.p: Shell said Monday it would allow independent observers to monitor the social and environmental impact of its giant Camisea gas project in Peru.

Shell, operator of the project with a 57.5 percent share in a consortium with Mobil, said it had reached agreement with Red Ambiental Peruana (RAP), an umbrella body grouping 35 non-governmental organisations.
The accord will enable teams of three-RAP nominated members, together with a representative of a native community, to inspect quarterly Shell's work in Peru's eastern jungle.
"We have invited RAP to challenge so that we can listen, adjust and improve," Shell Prospecting and Development (Peru) general manager Alan Hunt said.
Shell will transport the inspection teams to the Camisea region, which is situated in an environmentally diverse area inhabited by indigenous peoples.
"We will ensure that the social and environmental integrity of the zone is maintained," RAP president Eric Cardich said.

The Anglo-Dutch oil company hopes to start producing gas from Camisea's massive reserves -- estimated at 11 trillion cubic feet of natural gas and 600 million barrels of natural gas liquids -- as early as 1999.
Gas could be brought to the Peruvian capital Lima around 2002. Shell will be spending $125 million on the project this year, much of it on studies for the pipeline.
The first appraisal wells were drilled last month and if the Shell/Mobil consortium decide to proceed the project could last for 40 years and soak up $3.0 billion of foreign investment.

The fields hold six times the rest of Peru's hydrocarbon reserves, according to the government, which estimates it will receive $6 billion in tax revenue from Camisea during the first 30 years of operation.
